correctness.rationale: For nonzero singular A, every nontrivial idempotent E in EN=A must project onto im(A). Choosing its kernel complement K reduces nilpotency of the uniquely constrained N to y=-tr(A) and s x=-(tr(A))^2. This yields one completion for every complement when tr(A)=0, and for every complement except ker(A) when tr(A)≠0. The zero fiber is counted separately by image containment. Exact replay over q=2,3,4,5,7 and the global pair-count identity agree with the proof.

value.rationale: The recent literature makes the image set and its total cardinality a central invariant. Determining every fiber is the natural refinement and reveals a nonuniform multiplicity structure: zero, nonzero nilpotent, and nonnilpotent rank-one targets have distinct exact counts. The theorem is complete for every finite field rather than a small-q census.
